description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:592-603

```rust
pub struct MerkleAuditPath {
    pub leaf_index: u64,
    pub tree_size: u64,
    pub audit_path: Vec<[u8; 32]>,
}
```

Public fields with no constructor and no doc-comment about invariants.
A caller can build:

```rust
MerkleAuditPath { leaf_index: 0, tree_size: 0, audit_path: vec![] }
```

— `tree_size == 0` is malformed (rejected by `verify_inclusion` as
`Error::MerkleProofMalformed`).

```rust
MerkleAuditPath { leaf_index: 99, tree_size: 5, audit_path: vec![] }
```

— `leaf_index >= tree_size` (rejected at verify time).

```rust
MerkleAuditPath {
    leaf_index: 0,
    tree_size: 1024,
    audit_path: vec![[0;32]; 99],  // way more than ceil(log2(1024)) = 10
}
```

— overlong audit path (rejected at verify time).

ALL of these invariants are enforced at `verify_inclusion` time, not
at construction time. The contract is: the type's invariants are
"whatever `verify_inclusion` checks". Two problems:

A. A caller writing a `Display`-impl or a logging wrapper for
   `MerkleAuditPath` cannot tell from the type whether the values
   they're rendering are physically sensible.

B. A caller building a proof from raw u64s sourced from a CT log's
   JSON response cannot validate the proof structurally without
   running the full hash check. They want a constructor that returns
   `Result<Self>` so they can fail fast on malformed proofs without
   loading the leaf and root.

Recommendation: add `MerkleAuditPath::new(leaf_index, tree_size,
audit_path) -> Result<Self, Error>` that pre-validates the three
structural invariants (`tree_size > 0`, `leaf_index < tree_size`,
`audit_path.len() <= ceil(log2(tree_size))`). The slow hash check
still runs in `verify_inclusion`; the fast invariant check is just
moved earlier. Add `#[non_exhaustive]` (per PKIX-ppbr.15) so callers
must go through the constructor.

This is also a defensive-forcing concern: every caller currently
needs to re-implement the same three checks if they want them
pre-verify.

Priority P2; doesn't block correctness but does force caller-side
duplication.
title: MerkleAuditPath public fields admit invalid proofs — verify_inclusion is the only validator
